archetype.name: Dual-Threat (efficiency-first)
archetype.definition: A quarterback who now wins mostly with the ball out of his hand, on the league's best per-attempt efficiency, while still turning broken plays and a handful of designed runs into chunk yardage.

report.headline: Best per-throw passer in football this year, now sidelined by right-thumb surgery
report.take:
Before the thumb, Jackson was playing some of the cleanest football of his career. Across the snaps he played, he leads all 55 qualifiers in yards per attempt (9.97) and adjusted net yards per dropback (10.63), sits third in CPOE (8.29) and fourth in EPA per dropback (0.297). That is roughly a third of a point per dropback better than the league average. The low counting stats (193.4 passing yards a game, 27th) are not a knock. He threw only 19.4 times a game, Week 4 was a 52%-snap blowout, Week 8 ended after one snap, and a Ravens offense under new coach Jesse Minter runs at roughly a neutral pass rate.

The engine is accuracy on the short and middle levels, plus one receiver who turned his deep shots into points. On throws under 10 air yards he completed 82% at 0.362 EPA. The middle of the field produced 19.3 EPA and five of his six touchdowns. Zay Flowers drew 20 targets at 1.131 EPA per target, and those plays account for 22.6 of the 30.9 passing EPA. Mark Andrews saw more targets at a far ordinary 0.232. The legs are still there, though not as the volume runner of 2019: 10 scrambles for 107 yards and six first downs at 0.47 EPA each, and his 28.8 rushing yards a game rank sixth. The game-by-game line was sharpening, too. Bad-throw rate fell every week, from 25% to 10.5%, and CPOE climbed from 4.8 to 11.3.

What the numbers hide is how small and how lopsided the sample is. That is 97 attempts, and a CPOE 6.5 points above last season's 1.8, above even his 2024 peak. Only 18 deep throws carry a 0.64 EPA average built on 44% completions and Flowers. The money downs were flat. On third down he converted 34.8% at 0.044 EPA, although he faced an average of 9.2 yards to go. In the red zone his EPA was 0.037 and his CPOE was -7, with four touchdowns masking the inefficiency. The pocket numbers look better than his recent history: pressure-to-sack sits at 28%, against 43.9% last year. Weigh that as a hint rather than a reformed trait.

The outlook now hinges on the thumb, not the tape. He is on injured reserve after surgery on his right thumb, his throwing hand. He is listed fourth on the depth chart, with an estimated return of December 27, and the club has floated Week 16 against Cleveland as a possibility. Meanwhile the Ravens have cycled through Tyler Huntley, Joe Fagnano and Jacoby Brissett. When he does come back, the baseline is a very good efficiency passer with modest volume. Grip and ball placement in his first game back are the real unknown.

strengths.title: League-best yards per throw
strengths.body: He leads all qualifiers in YPA and adjusted net yards per dropback. That comes from high-percentage throws inside 10 yards plus a deep game that paid off when it hit. Some regression is coming, but his 8.44 YPA last year (sixth) shows the yards-per-attempt profile is real, not a four-game fluke.

strengths.title: Short and middle accuracy
strengths.body: He completed 79.6% of throws at 0–9 air yards, and the middle of the field produced five touchdowns at a CPOE of 11.9. The bad-throw rate trended down every week he played a full game. The accuracy is a genuine strength, but the level is inflated by a small sample, so expect it to settle toward his 2024 form rather than hold at 8+ CPOE.

strengths.title: Scrambles that move chains
strengths.body: Ten scrambles produced 107 yards and six first downs at 0.47 EPA apiece. That pays for the 3.11-second time to throw that comes with extending plays. He is no longer the 1,000-yard runner of his early years, but 28.8 rushing yards a game, sixth at the position, still gives him a reliable second scoring channel.

concerns.title: Surgery on his throwing thumb
concerns.body: He is on injured reserve after surgery on his right thumb. The estimated return is late December, and the team only says there is a chance at Week 16. Even if he makes it back, a throwing-hand repair is exactly the kind of injury that can dull the touch and placement his season was built on. He may get only a couple of games before the year ends.

concerns.title: Small sample, career-high accuracy
concerns.body: His 97 attempts carry a CPOE far above both last season and any year in his career. A large share of the passing EPA came on Flowers' 20 targets. That points to regression in completion rate and deep efficiency, though from a level well above average. The 18 deep attempts at 0.64 EPA are the most fragile piece.

concerns.title: Flat on third down, red zone
concerns.body: Third downs produced 0.044 EPA and a 34.8% conversion rate, though he faced long yardage (9.2 to go on average). Red-zone passing ran a CPOE of -7, and four touchdowns hid that. The splits are small, but this is where his low passing volume also limits his scoring ceiling.

trend.note: Passing EPA ran 8.7, 2.3, 10.2 and 10.1 over his four full games, with CPOE rising each week and bad throws falling. Then Week 8 ended after one snap, and right-thumb surgery put him on IR.

nextGame.headline: Jackson is out; Ravens visit Houston as 6.5-point underdogs
nextGame.body:
Jackson will not play Week 12. He is on injured reserve after thumb surgery and listed fourth on the depth chart, so this game bears on him only through the team he returns to. Houston would have been an interesting test for him. Its defense ranks third in sack rate and sixth in success rate allowed, but 31st in explosive pass rate. That is the profile a deep-accurate, play-extending quarterback can punish. A backup who holds the ball is far more likely to be sacked than to hit those chunk plays.

On availability, Houston is without edge rusher Danielle Hunter (76% of snaps), and defensive tackle Sheldon Rankins is questionable. That softens the pass rush for whoever starts for Baltimore. The Book has Houston -6.5 with a 46.5 total and Baltimore at +251, which reflects the Ravens' quarterback situation. For Jackson's own outlook, the news to watch is his practice status in the coming weeks, not this score.

keyMatchups.title: Jackson's availability timeline
keyMatchups.body: He is on IR with an estimated return of December 27, and the team calls Week 16 possible. Every week until then is a backup start. His rest-of-season value rests on practice reports, not matchups.

keyMatchups.title: Houston's pass rush vs Baltimore line
keyMatchups.body: Houston gets home at the third-best sack rate. Baltimore's line ranks 24th in hit rate allowed, even with Jackson's scrambling. Hunter's absence trims the threat, but this remains a long day for a less mobile quarterback.

keyMatchups.title: Explosive passes there to take
keyMatchups.body: Houston allows the second-most explosive passes in the league, and its WR2 role gives up 0.51 EPA a target. Flowers was Jackson's big-play outlet at 1.131 EPA a target. Whether a backup can find him downfield decides whether Baltimore keeps pace.

nextGame.watch: Whether Jackson returns to practice with his right thumb in the next two weeks, the first real signal on a Week 16 return.

restOfSeason.body:
Best case, Jackson returns for Week 16 against Cleveland and plays out the schedule. Even then, that is a small window. More likely he gets one or two games, and the first may come with a protected throwing hand and a conservative plan. When he plays, expect the same shape: modest attempts in a balanced offense, strong per-throw efficiency, and steady scramble yardage. Project something like 175–235 passing yards, 1–1.8 touchdowns and 18–35 rushing yards a game.

What holds up is the yards-per-attempt profile and the scramble value, both backed by recent seasons. What should give back is the career-high CPOE, the deep-ball EPA built on 18 attempts, and the pressure-to-sack rate, which ran far better than his 2023–25 norm. A rusty or tentative return would hit the deep game first.
swingFactors: Whether he returns by Week 16 or later
Grip and accuracy after right-thumb surgery

confidence.note: 97 attempts, throwing-hand surgery, and an uncertain return date that leaves few games.
